letter.subject: Concern about cookie and tracking practices on intertek.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns about cookie and tracking practices on https://intertek.com.

The concerns below arise from an automated, passive audit carried out on 2026-11-08 04:12 UTC using a fresh browser. The audit detected the cookie banner, clicked “Reject All”, then visited https://www.intertek.com/industries/, https://www.intertek.com/industries-services/, and https://www.intertek.com/chemicals/, while recording what cookies were set and what requests were still sent.

1. Our review suggests the observed tracking conflicts with your privacy policy’s stated consent requirement. Your policy says: “By using this Platform, we are seeking to obtain your consent to use these various cookies.” However, the audit recorded advertising identifiers being sent before the banner was answered and after “Reject All” was clicked, including to Google and Facebook.

2. Before any choice was made on the banner, the following advertising cookies were already set: _fbp; _ga and _ga_2NP31Y6QYW; and __cf_bm, bcookie, li_gc, lidc. These appeared to contain unique identifiers.

3. After “Reject All” was clicked, advertising-related requests were still sent to Microsoft (16 requests to licdn.com and linkedin.com), Facebook (11 requests to facebook.com and facebook.net), and Google (10 requests to googletagmanager.com).

4. After rejection, the value of _fbp, described by the audit as an identifier unique to that browser, was sent to facebook.com in the request address.

5. Before the banner was answered, the value of _ga, described by the audit as an identifier unique to that browser, was sent to doubleclick.net and google.co.uk in the request address.

6. Our review also suggests there may be a transparency issue. The privacy policy reviewed at https://www.intertek.com/privacy-policy/ names 0 companies, while the audit observed Facebook, Google and Microsoft receiving data.

Please:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential cookies or tracking operating before consent or after rejection.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter cannot be resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
